gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the four phono stages' MC specs side by side in common units. Marantz MODEL 30 is the only one whose MC input load can be changed (33, 100 or 390 Ω). Luxman L-505Z is fixed at 100 Ω and Musical Fidelity A1 at 1 kΩ, and Rega Elex Mk4 has no MC input at all. The A1 also needs 450 µV where the Marantz needs 250 µV, which is 5.1 dB more input from the cartridge.
standout_why: I read Rhythm Audio's Darko piece on the L-505Z (cited). It gives 100 W into 8 Ω and that it was tested with two MC turntables, but no phono gain, load or sensitivity. Luxman's own L-505Z page (cited) lists only Luxman's figures. I could not compare against the What Hi-Fi best-buys page or the Elex Mk4 review (both came back with no body text), or against Stereophile Recommended Components (HTTP 403). ChatGPT's own answer already calls the MODEL 30 the 'best for moving-coil cartridges' with 'multiple MC settings', so the direction is already out there. What's new is the actual load values, the fixed loads on the Luxman and A1, and the sensitivity difference in dB.
decides: This confirms the MODEL 30 for MC owners and adds a footnote to the other picks. The A1's fixed 1 kΩ MC load and 450 µV sensitivity suit higher-output MC cartridges better than low-output, low-impedance ones. The L-505Z gives a single 100 Ω load. The Elex Mk4 needs a separate phono stage for any MC cartridge. The phono S/N numbers shouldn't be ranked against each other: Luxman's 70 dB MC figure is IHF-A weighted, while Marantz (75 dB) and Musical Fidelity (70 dB) give no weighting or reference level on their pages.
